title: fix(objectql): bucket a declared Field.date by its calendar day under every timezone (#24618)
body:
Fixes #24618

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

A non-UTC `timezone` forces `engine.aggregate` onto the in-memory rows path (ADR-0053 Phase 2). On that path `projectGroupValue` passed every date-bucketed value to `bucketDateKey` together with the zone. It had no `date` / `datetime` branch. `bucketDateKey` takes an INSTANT, so it read `'2026-10-01'` as `2026-10-01T00:00Z` and placed it on the zone's calendar. In every zone west of UTC, a `Field.date` therefore landed one day early. The SQL pushdown path, which runs only at UTC, labelled the stored day. Measured at bucketDateKey on the base `973917c57`: `'2026-10-01'` under America/New_York gives `2026-09-30 / 2026-W40 / 2026-09 / 2026-Q3 / 2026`. America/Los_Angeles gives the same. UTC and Asia/Tokyo give `2026-10-01 / 2026-W40 / 2026-10 / 2026-Q4 / 2026`. A `Date` at that day's UTC midnight shifts the same way.

## The fix

- `packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts`: `applyInMemoryAggregation` already receives the object's declared field map, because `engine.aggregate` passes `declaredFields`. Two new internal helpers (neither is exported):
  - `calendarDayGroupFields` reads which date-bucketed `groupBy` fields the object declares a calendar day. It reads them once per call, from the declaration, through `declaredFieldClasses` (class `date`, that is, `CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES`).
  - `bucketCalendarDay` puts such a value through `temporalStorageForm(value, 'date')`, the one storage rule. It then labels the value with `bucketDateKey` and no zone.
- Fields that keep today's zone path:
  - a `datetime`;
  - any field the declaration cannot type: no `fields` argument, an undeclared field, or a `formula`.
- `packages/core/src/utils/datetime.ts`: comment only. `bucketDateKey`'s docblock now says that `value` is an instant, and that a caller bucketing a `date` passes no zone.
- No exported signature changes and no new export. The built `.d.ts` still reads `bucketDateKey(value, granularity, timezone?)`, `bucketDateValue(value, granularity, timezone?)` and `applyInMemoryAggregation(rows, ast, timezone?, fields?, reportWithheld?)`. Neither helper appears in any `.d.ts` as a declaration.

Where it lands: the field type was already available inside `packages/objectql`, so `packages/services/service-analytics` needs no change. The cube path reaches this function through `ObjectQLStrategy`, then `ctx.executeAggregate`, then `engine.aggregate`, then `applyInMemoryAggregation(raw, ast, tz, declaredFields)`. `dataset-executor.ts` passes its timezone into the same `engine.aggregate`.

## Fixture triage

`packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-timezone.test.ts` declared `closed_at` a `date`, but its rows hold instants such as `2024-03-01T03:00:00.000Z`, and its case pins the New York shift.
- Disposition: the declaration is corrected to `datetime`, the type of what the rows store. The file keeps pinning the routing it is about, and the new file pins the `date` reading.
- I scanned every test that combines a date bucket with a non-UTC zone: 7 files. The other six use mocks, refusals or totals only, and none of them changes.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-timezone.dogfood.test.ts` buckets `created_at`. The registry injects that field as a `datetime`, so it is unaffected.

## Tests

New file `packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation-date-calendar-day.test.ts`, 30 cases. All expected labels are written as literals.
- **(a)** A declared `date` equals the stored days under America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, UTC and Asia/Tokyo, at day, week, month, quarter and year. The fixture covers these edges:
  - a quarter start (10-01);
  - two ISO-week Mondays (10-05, 11-02);
  - a month start on a Sunday (11-01);
  - a year start in the previous year's W53 (2027-01-01);
  - an unset day.

  Also in (a):
  - the door's expected month `{2026-10: 6, 2026-11: 4}` and quarter `{2026-Q4: 10}` under New York;
  - a `Date` value at UTC midnight buckets by its UTC day;
  - an `alias` does not change which field's declaration is read.
- **(b)** Control: a declared `datetime` under New York still lands on the New York day. `2026-10-01T02:00Z` gives `2026-09-30` and quarter `2026-Q3`. Under UTC the same instants land on the UTC day.
- **(c)** `engine.aggregate`: the pushdown route and the rows route give the same labels for a `date`. The pushdown route runs at UTC; a driver double answers the literal labels and counts its native calls. The rows route runs under each non-UTC zone.

**Ablation.** The fix was committed first (`3e648b2eb`). `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` then replaced `calendarDayFields.has(field)` with `false`: anchor 1 to 0, blob `2f518a44` to `ca64430f`. After restore, the blob equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Predicted: (a) red under New York and Los Angeles, green under UTC and Tokyo; (b) green; (c) red.
- Observed: **18 failed / 14 passed**, over the new file plus `engine-aggregate-timezone.test.ts`. The 18 are the 13 New York / Los Angeles cases of (a) and the 5 of (c). For the door case, the received month under the mutation was `{2026-09: 1, 2026-10: 6, 2026-11: 3}`.
- Green: (b), the UTC and Tokyo cases, and the routing file.
- The suite imports `./in-memory-aggregation.js` relatively, so the mutation ran against `src` and needed no build leg.

**Real-SQL parity.** This was a one-off measurement and is not committed.
- Setup: `@objectstack/driver-sql` (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`) built in this worktree, with `@objectstack/objectql` built at `d789f7e23`. Same 12 rows, `due_date` declared `date`.
- `driver.aggregate` (the real SQL) against `applyInMemoryAggregation(find(), ast, tz, fields)`, for New York, Los Angeles and Tokyo at all five granularities: **15/15 agree**.
- Control leg, the same call without the field map (the zone path the code took before): **10/15 disagree**. Those are New York and Los Angeles at all five granularities; Tokyo agrees.
- `engine.aggregate` over the same `SqlDriver`, UTC (real pushdown) against each non-UTC zone (rows route): **15/15 agree**.
- SQLite's `find()` presented the `date` column as a `string`. driver-memory's `find()` returned both a string write and a `Date` write as a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string. It advertises no native granularity, so its `date` buckets always take this path.

**Runs:**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 448 files / 8444 tests passed at `d789f7e23`. `src` is unchanged since then; only the new test file's typing changed. Re-run at `bf7b57a5d`: the new file plus the routing file, 2 files / 32 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` (tsc plus `check:test-typecheck`, whose program lists both test files) exited 0 at `bf7b57a5d`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck` and its local tests (106 files / 2580 tests) passed at `d789f7e23`.
- Local gate union at `bf7b57a5d`: 68 derived commands (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`), 67 exit 0. `node scripts/check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` exited 2: it refuses on a shallow clone, and the deepening fetch was cut off by the proxy (`fatal: early EOF`), so it is NOT MEASURED. `--ran` reconciliation: 68 derived, 68 run, 0 unrun. Not run locally, left to CI: the `repo` vitest project (`test:repo`), the workspace type-check lanes, and the families the derivation names as outside its list.

## Not in this PR: the parity gate's non-UTC probe

`packages/verify/src/date-bucket-parity.ts` belongs to `domain:cli` and was not edited. It calls `applyInMemoryAggregation(rows, ast)` with no zone and no field map, so it cannot see this class. To see it, the `on` column (`Field.date`) needs a second comparison: the same pushed-down answer against `applyInMemoryAggregation(rows, ast, 'America/New_York', FIELDS)`, plus a positive-offset zone. A `date` pushdown answer has no zone. The probe's existing `on` values `2024-07-01` and `2025-01-01` already cross a quarter edge and a year edge under New York. This half of the card's "expected fix shape" goes to that lane through the seat.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-analytics.ts`, `MemoryAnalyticsService.aggregateWithTimeBuckets`, calls `bucketDateKey(value, granularity, timezone)` with no `date` / `datetime` branch. That is the same class of defect. No stock composition registers `MemoryAnalyticsService`: it is exported, and `service-analytics` names it only as a fallback a host supplies. I measured no reach, so nothing is filed. Owner: none.
- `engine.aggregate` still forces the rows route for any non-UTC zone, even when every date-bucketed item is a declared `date`, whose pushdown answer does not depend on the zone. This is a performance note, not a defect, and nothing pulls on it.
- A `formula` whose result is a date stays on the zone path, because its declaration names no stored value class.
